text: Sage reveals focus of training ahead of Hoffenheim Skip navigation Shop Tickets Login Crystal palace News Matches Palace TV Crystal palace News Matches Palace TV Teams Shop Tickets Login Crystal palace Login Login Sage reveals focus of training ahead of Hoffenheim First-team 1 day ago Crystal Palace must rediscover the balance between offensive and defensive proficiency when they take on TSG Hoffenheim on Thursday evening (17:45 GMT). Book tickets That is the view of Manager Pierre Sage who – speaking in his pre-match press conference ahead of the UEFA Europa League match at Selhurst Park, for which tickets are still on sale – is hoping his side can return to winning ways in continental competition. Palace began their maiden Europa League voyage with three points and a 4-0 win against Lech Poznań at Selhurst Park last time out, but have found clean sheets more difficult to come by since, despite some strong defending against Fulham and Tottenham Hotspur last week. Finding the balance between their early-season attacking form, and recent defensive improvement, has been the focus of Palace’s increased number of training sessions this week, according to the Manager. “The responsibility is on me and I have to deal with this kind of thing,” Sage said. “And from Monday to today, the work was really at a good level. “We worked a lot on things which we could not work on for a long time, because of the games after games, and that was a good sign because the players played the way we decided and with a lot of efficiency. “[We trained] especially offensively, the way to build up in our play, in the way to play in the back of the last line of the opponent. “I think in our two last games we defended a lot, more or less well, but we didn't attack in the way that we decided before the game. And that's why we have to come back to this, by finding the balance between the two. “I only know that we need to win games. In my last experience in the Europa League [with Lyon], I lost only one. For the moment, we lost one and we made the draw. If we win two or three games again, we can qualify. That's the most important objective for the moment. “We have to be focused on that. We know that we will play a different football [style], a different kind of team, and maybe with the games and the situation of every opponent, it could be different because some of them could maybe be qualified quickly and some could be eliminated quickly. “That's why we have to capitalise and to take the points that we need.” Quote Icons We enjoy playing and I think it's one of the best things to do in life, play a match of football — Pierre Sage Palace have won just two of their last seven matches in all competitions – a busy run of fixtures since 11th October – but Sage noted: “When we play, it's always a good thing. “We enjoy playing and I think it's one of the best things to do in life, play a match of football. We have big chances this year, we play every three days and for the moment the results are not at the level of our entertainment to play, but we have to consider that the performances will come if we work, if we continue in our process. “With time, as I told you, I think the play and the results will be better and we will enjoy playing every three days more. “If we, as a staff and players, didn't give our lives every day, I would not be optimistic. But I am optimistic because I see, every day, every player on the pitch really involved in the work. “If you do that day after day, I'm sure good things will happen. That's why I'm always optimistic when I see this kind of thing.” Match Details Crystal Palace v TSG Hoffenheim Thursday, 5th November 17:45 GMT UEFA Europa League Selhurst Park Tickets available here . text: Team News: Updates on Timber & Strand Larsen Skip navigation Shop Tickets Login Crystal palace News Matches Palace TV Crystal palace News Matches Palace TV Teams Shop Tickets Login Crystal palace Login Login Team News: Updates on Timber & Strand Larsen First-team 1 day ago Crystal Palace’s busy run of fixtures continues when Pierre Sage’s side host TSG Hoffenheim on Thursday (5th November, 17:45 GMT) – with the Eagles boosted by a pre-match team news update. The match, for which tickets remain on sale , will see Palace look to build on four points from their opening three league phase matches in the UEFA Europa League. And the team will be bolstered by the return of both midfielder Quinten Timber and forward Jørgen Strand Larsen , both injured since the Eagles’ last European match away at Beșiktaș. Sage told his pre-match press conference: “Both [players] will be back with us. “They were training with us last week but not ready to play, but now they are ready to play. “All [others] will be okay.” The match is Palace’s eighth in the space of 25 days since 11th October, with the Eagles also competing in both the Premier League and Carabao Cup. Sage said of preparations: “First of all it’s exciting, because if we play in a European cup, it’s because the team did well last year and won the Conference League. We have to deal with that but it’s a good thing. “To deal with three different competitions, for the process, it’s always the same because we prepare in the same way. “The difference between the three competitions is the time we have before the games to prepare. This time we have three sessions before the game, one more than the two [games] before, and that’s really important because we need time to work, especially when we’re in our situation. “What we did during these sessions was really important for the confidence of the players, for their understanding of the gameplan, and for their capacity to apply it.” Buy tickets Match Details Crystal Palace v TSG Hoffenheim Thursday, 5th November 17:45 GMT UEFA Europa League Selhurst Park Related News First-team Match previews Related News More News

Another Home Win: We Confidently Defeated Paks Ferencvaros defeated Paks 2–0 at Groupama Arena in the 12th round of the OTP Bank Liga. ferencváros Paks otp bank liga Following a classic domestic match, our men’s soccer team took the field again on Sunday at Groupama Arena for Matchday 12 of the OTP Bank Liga. In the previous round, we secured a commanding victory in the eternal derby against MTK, earning our first home win of the season. The question, then, was whether we could continue our strong performance at home and secure all three points once again. Head coach Balázs Borbély entrusted this task to the very same starting eleven that had kicked off the successful match the previous week: Dibusz, Osváth, Raemaekers, Gómez, Cadu – Maiga, Madarász – Zachariassen, Corbu, Birmancsevics – Yusuf. A Fradi victory would not only mean securing the three points but also that the two teams—of which Paks had played one more game—would swap places in the standings, with Ferencváros moving up to third place. First Half It became clear within the first five minutes that György Bognár, the head coach of Paks, had also set his team’s goal as securing three points; the visiting green-and-whites, playing in black, opened the match with considerable intensity. The first major scoring opportunity, however, arose in front of their own goal. In the 7th minute, Birmancsevics broke through alone toward the goal, but his shot from the corner of the box was stopped by goalkeeper Gyetván. After that, fans had to wait until the 20th minute for the next noteworthy event, when Madarász grew tired of the fruitless scramble in front of the goal and blasted a shot at the Paks goal from 20 meters out—still to no avail. Corbu’s attempt from the right corner of the penalty area a minute later yielded the same result. Ferencváros’s dominance on the field, which had become clear by the middle of the half, thus remained fruitless for the time being. This was also the case after the long-range attempt that followed, this time by Maiga, who shot from twenty-five yards out, but Gyetván made another confident save. Midway through the half, Birmancsevics showed off his footwork near the corner flag, but his display of skill did not lead to a scoring opportunity. Meanwhile, Paks could only muster the energy for the occasional counterattack that fizzled out. In the 43rd minute, following a corner kick, Raemaekers’ header sailed just over the crossbar before the remaining minutes of the first half ticked away. The teams went into halftime scoreless. Second Half Balázs Borbély sent his team out with the same lineup for the second half. Not only did Birmancsevics stay on the field, but in the 47th minute, he also dribbled past his defender from the left just centimeters in front of the penalty area—as confirmed by the VAR review—resulting in a free kick from a promising position instead of a penalty kick, though no goal came of it.  Nor did the next cross from Birmancsevics, which Zachariassen shot toward the goal from five meters with a half-turn, and which Gyetván saved with a brilliant dive. Shortly afterward, he did the same with a header by Gómez following a free kick. During this period, play was practically confined to Paks’s penalty area. Then, in the 59th minute, the goal finally came. Corbu cut in from the left wing, and his pinpoint cross was met by Yusuf, who arrived at just the right moment and nodded the ball unstoppably into the net from six meters out with equally pinpoint accuracy (1–0). The match became increasingly one-sided, with Fradi’s attacks continuing and Paks defending with growing desperation. Aside from the visiting goalkeeper’s spectacular saves, the only other notable events were that Yusuf first picked up a yellow card and then, in the 71st minute, was substituted for a well-deserved rest; Joseph replaced him on the field, just as Bero, returning from injury, replaced Madarász. In a match that eventually became one-sided, Fradi created chance after chance, but sometimes we lacked focus, and other times Gyetván pulled off a last-minute save. And just when everyone had written off the game as a one-goal victory for FTC, Fradi managed one more spectacular moment. In the 94th minute, Cadu crossed from the left into the middle, and although Joseph hit the left post from five meters out, Zachariassen blasted home the rebound (2–0). There wasn’t even time for a restart, and Ferencváros secured its second home victory of the season with a confident performance. The next match is on Thursday at 6:45 p.m. away against AC Milan in the UEFA Europa League. Madarász (Bero, 71.), Maiga (Á. Nagy, 80.) – Zachariassen, Corbu, Birmancsevics (Levi, 89.) – Yusuf (Joseph, 71.). Paksi FC : Gyetván – Győrfi (Wiesner, 60'), Lenzsér, Kinyik, Vécsei, Silye – M. Football October 22. 2026. Win by a landslide again in the UEL! Ferencvaros defeated SCU Torreense 4-1 in the third round of the Europa League group stage. UEFA Europa League Torreense On Thursday evening, our men’s soccer team hosted USC Torreense—a Portuguese second-division side and Portuguese Cup champion—at Groupama Arena in the third round of the UEFA Europa League group stage. For the second home match of the group stage of the 2026–2027 season, head coach Balázs Borbély kept young Dániel Radnóti in goal and selected the following starting lineup: Radnóti – O. Nagy, Gómez, Zohoré, O’Dowda – Madarász, Á. Nagy, Zachariassen – Birmancsevics, Arzani, Yusuf. First Half In the minutes following the opening whistle, it would have been difficult for an outsider to tell which team was the home side and which was the visiting team, as both sides threw themselves into the game with roughly the same intensity, mostly in the middle third of the field. In the 5th minute, Radnóti did have to make a save on a moderately powerful shot, but this posed no problem for our young goalkeeper. The same scenario repeated itself in the 11th minute, following a series of midfield exchanges that culminated in the referee issuing a yellow card to Zachariassen with a fairly light hand. Our response to all this was a header by Yusuf, which sailed just centimeters over the crossbar. At the end of the first quarter-hour, it was Yusuf’s turn again; this time, he sent a low cross sailing over the goal. In the 20th minute, however, he showed no mercy: he gratefully accepted the gift of the ball, drove forward, and fired a low shot into the net from 16 meters out (1-0)! Unfortunately, the response wasn’t long in coming, and this time it was our defense that gave away the goal. In the 23rd minute, Pozo received a low cross from the left between three of our defenders, with his back to the goal; he then, leaning backward, curled the ball into the left corner with a half-turn (1-1). In the final quarter-hour of the first half, the teams essentially replicated the first half. The match was dominated primarily by physical battles, with the goals rarely facing any real danger. The only truly noteworthy moment came when O’Dowda headed Ádám Nagy’s cross over the bar from practically right in front of the goal. We went into halftime tied. Second Half At halftime, Balázs Borbély saw no reason to make any substitutions, so we continued the game with the same lineup we started with. And with roughly the same intensity as well. However, this intensity continued to be focused more on physical battles than on creating truly dangerous scoring opportunities. Both teams spent the first ten minutes of the half jostling for position. Our head coach grew tired of this the quickest and responded to what had happened so far by bringing on Madarász for Corbu. It was magical. What happened immediately afterward was pure magic: in the 58th minute, following a Birmancsevics corner, Gómez Mariano rose from a standing position in a manner that would put helicopters to shame, and despite being tugged at, he slid the ball under the crossbar with unyielding precision (2–1)! Torreense coach Luís Tralhaó had only one response to our lead: he, too, tried making substitutions. With significantly less success than his Ferencváros counterpart. The rest of the match clearly demonstrated this. In the 63rd minute, Alfaro and Zoabi left the field, replaced by Jean and Jatta; then, in the 74th minute, Drammeh and goal-scorer Pozo were substituted for Abubakari and Quintero. A minute after this substitution, Balázs Borbély demonstrated how to make an effective substitution. Joseph and Maiga came on for the departing Yusuf and Arzani. The latter soon took center stage. In the 80th minute, O’Dowda delivered a superb cross; Maiga met it perfectly and, with a little help from his defender, curled it into the net (3-1)! The fact that the goal was officially credited to Diadié did nothing to dampen the joy. And that wasn’t the end of it. The final blow came in the 89th minute, once again from the substitutes. Joseph won the ball and passed it to Lisztes, who had come on just two minutes earlier; Lisztes then curled a superb shot into the net (4-1)—the game was decided! Our team delivered a sensational second-half performance to crush Torrense and win its third group-stage match! Ferencváros now stands with 3 wins and 9 points after three rounds in the UEFA Europa League! The action continues in two weeks, on November 5, when we visit Italian side AC Milan. For ticket information on Ferencváros’s upcoming home games, please visit the Groupama Arena ticket offices (general hours: Mon.: Closed, Mon–Fri: 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m., Sat: 9:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m. (on match days, until kickoff), Sun: Closed, except on match days) or our ticket sales website, meccsjegy.fradi.hu! text: Bayer 04 Leverkusen Fußball GmbH | bayer04.de Europa League Ahead of Marseille match: Martínez sees upturn at OM – Medina on key fac­tors against for­mer club The Europa League campaign continues: Bayer 04 host Olympique Marseille at the BayArena on matchday four of the group stage on Thursday 5 November (kick-off: 21:00 CET). Ahead of the clash against the club from the French Mediterranean coast, head coach Carles Martínez spoke about the visitors’ form and had some good news regarding the squad. Former OM player Facundo Medina spoke, amongst other things, about the factors that will be crucial against his old club. Show more Europa League Our next oppo­nents: Marseille on the up, but still struggling in the Europa League Olympique Marseille are really hitting their stride in Ligue 1. The nine-time French champions have fought their way back after a mixed start to the season and recently recorded four wins in a row. However, OM have no points in the Europa League so far this term. On Thursday, 5 November (kick-off: 21:00 CET), Marseille will be looking to change that at the BayArena. The lowdown on our next opponents.
